extracted.intended_audience: NASA Headquarters staff preparing correspondence (action offices, OCIC, signers) for the Office of the Administrator
extracted.subtask_description: Standards and mandatory procedures for preparing, formatting, routing, safeguarding, and filing correspondence (letters, memos, signature packages) for officials in NASA's Office of the Administrator.

rubrics_metrics.name: Classified-material outer/inner envelope handling
rubrics_metrics.description: Use two envelopes. The outside envelope must conform to NPR instructions. The inner envelope must have both addresses as shown on the outer envelope, plus the overall classification of the document being transferred.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Mark the classification level on the front and back top, and bottom of the envelope. The inner envelope must show both addresses and the overall classification; place classification mark on front and back and top and bottom.

rubrics_metrics.name: Classified-material receipts and tracing
rubrics_metrics.description: Attach a classified material receipt (NASA Form 387) to the inner envelope for the addressee to sign and return to your activity to confirm receipt.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If receipt is not confirmed within 20 days, initiate tracer action and, if unresolved, contact the Center's Security Office. For Top Secret material, follow NPD 1620.2A or contact Center Security Office for specific instructions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Internal handling of classified documents
rubrics_metrics.description: When taking classified documents outside the work area, carry them in a sealed, opaque envelope to prevent advertising that you are carrying classified material.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When using classified material within the work space, place a classified cover sheet on the document if it is outside of the container (for example, on your desk).

rubrics_metrics.name: External (offsite) hand-carry of classified documents
rubrics_metrics.description: If required to hand-carry classified documents outside of a NASA Center, you must receive a briefing and a courier card from your Center's Security Office before being approved to take classified documents offsite.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not hand-carry classified material offsite without the required briefing and courier authorization.

rubrics_metrics.name: Administrator correspondence: clarity, concision, and page limit
rubrics_metrics.description: Prepare correspondence for signature of officials in the Office of the Administrator in a clear, direct, and concise style and confine to one page whenever possible.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If additional information is essential, develop it in an enclosure.

rubrics_metrics.name: Letter format for Administrator correspondence
rubrics_metrics.description: Letters should be prepared in the modified semiblock style, indenting paragraphs five spaces.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not right-justify margins. See Appendix A, Figure A-1 for examples and signature block placement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Memorandum format for Administrator correspondence
rubrics_metrics.description: Prepare memos in block style, following the general guidelines outlined in Chapter 4: Memorandums (see Appendix A, Figure A-2).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not right-justify margins.

rubrics_metrics.name: Approval memos content
rubrics_metrics.description: When requesting approval of officials in the Office of the Administrator, prepare a memo for the official's signature containing the proposed response.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow the example/format in Appendix A, Figure A-3.

rubrics_metrics.name: Stationery requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: Use Office of the Administrator's letterhead for preparing letters and memos for the signature of officials in the Office of the Administrator.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Administrator's letterhead is available from the OCIC or from the GSFC Supply Center through designated code-specific authorizing officials (usually the lead secretary of the code).

rubrics_metrics.name: Type and font
rubrics_metrics.description: Use any font for the Administrator's correspondence that is easy to read.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Suggested fonts are courier, times new roman, or arial, ranging in sizes from 10 to 12.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reply-to/office-code on Administrator letterhead
rubrics_metrics.description: The Administrator's letterhead does not contain a 'Reply to Attn of:' line.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not show the originating office's code and mail stop on either original memos or letters.

rubrics_metrics.name: Dating correspondence
rubrics_metrics.description: Do not date the letter or memo.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Correspondence is date stamped in either the Administrator's office or OCIC.

rubrics_metrics.name: Salutation guidance
rubrics_metrics.description: Use the models of addresses and proper salutations listed in Appendix E.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For addresses not listed or if in doubt as to proper salutation or complimentary close, contact the OCIC.

rubrics_metrics.name: Complimentary close and signature block placement
rubrics_metrics.description: Type the complimentary close and signature block on letters five spaces to the right of the center.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See section 17 (Signature Blocks) of Appendix A and Figure A-1 for examples showing proper complimentary close and signature blocks for officials in the Office of the Administrator.

rubrics_metrics.name: OCIC required file copies (three-copy rule)
rubrics_metrics.description: The OCIC requires three file copies: Yellow official file copy (showing concurring initials, NASA Form 1267), White file copy (OCIC file copy, plain bond), White file copy (letterhead copy) stamped and returned to Action Office as its official file copy.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The OCIC will dispatch the original. If no envelope is present in the signature package, the original will be mailed by the Action Office. For addressees outside NASA Headquarters, include properly addressed envelopes (see paragraph 13.c).

rubrics_metrics.name: Distribution-of-copies minimization and cc/bcc rules
rubrics_metrics.description: Keep reproduction and distribution of information copies to the minimum required. Type cc's on the original only when necessary for a recipient to know who received copies. Type bcc's on file copies only.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: After signature, the OCIC will return a photocopied original to the action office for distribution to cc's, or if no cc's are required, this photocopy will serve as a record of the signature. Bcc's include all concurring officials and individuals who received a copy of the incoming document; after obtaining signature the OCIC will return a file copy to the preparing office for reproduction and internal NASA distribution.

rubrics_metrics.name: Administrator's control number and suspense date marking
rubrics_metrics.description: Show the Administrator's control number and suspense date on all file and internal information copies (bcc's).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not include any of this identifying information on cc's or copies going outside NASA.

rubrics_metrics.name: Identification line for office/writer/typist and rewritten/retyped notation
rubrics_metrics.description: Include identification of office, writer, and typist with date and phone extension in the header/filer line.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: BPM/RFJones:pld:12/12/92:4831; If rewritten or retyped show 'Rewritten:' or 'Retyped:' with the new identification line.

rubrics_metrics.name: Action Document Summary (ADS) requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Use NHQ Form 117, Action Document Summary, to summarize important aspects of the letter or memo submitted for signature.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: ADS guidelines: type legibly (neat corrections acceptable); type on the original form or on a reproduced copy; limit to one page (if two pages use plain bond for second); write in active voice. The original ADS is retained by OCIC; a copy is returned to the originator.

rubrics_metrics.name: Assembly for signature: required components and packaging
rubrics_metrics.description: When the letter is ready for final review and signature, assemble it with mandatory supplies and forms as outlined.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Mandatory supplies: one lavender folder (signature packages only), ADS (NHQ Form 117), Signature and Incoming Tab (NASA Form 422), Concurrence and Background Tab (NASA Form 423), Enclosure(s) Tab (Form 1658), Executive Correspondence Cover, four binder clips. Preaddressed envelopes (appropriate size) are included to mail originals to addressees outside NASA; address envelopes properly with office code of signer indicated in top left corner. If the letter has enclosures, attach an extra set to the official file copy. (For signature packages containing directives see separate instructions.)

rubrics_metrics.name: Routing time and hand-carry responsibility
rubrics_metrics.description: The Action Office is responsible for hand-carrying Administrator's signature packages between all offices for concurrences and ultimately to the OCIC.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The package should not remain in any one office for more than 24 hours and should reach the OCIC prior to the suspense date.

rubrics_metrics.name: Control responsibilities of Headquarters offices for Administrator correspondence
rubrics_metrics.description: Each Headquarters Office must establish and maintain a control system for flow of Office of the Administrator correspondence and perform reviews and hand-carry duties.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specific responsibilities: establish/maintain control system; review incoming documents to ensure action assigned to appropriate person/office; ensure response deadlines appropriate and met; review signature package to ensure guidelines of Appendix have been met; hand-carry documents to OCIC for signature and dispatch.

rubrics_metrics.name: Coordination of assigned actions (reassignments, suspenses, interim/telephone replies)
rubrics_metrics.description: Procedures for reassigning actions, extending/canceling suspense requirements, preparing interim replies, documenting telephone replies, and changing the designation of signing officials.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reassigning Action: contact code-specific analyst immediately for reassignment. Extending/Cancelling Suspense: review immediately; if extension required, telephone OCIC or state reasons on a routing slip (NASA Form 26) and forward to OCIC for concurrence. Interim Reply: prepare interim reply acknowledging receipt and stating when final reply expected; furnish copy to OCIC prior to original suspense date. Telephone Reply: forward a routing slip (NASA Form 26) or email analyst stating 'Handled by telephone conversation between (NASA official) and (addressee) on (date)' with brief summary. Change in Designation of Signing Official: request in writing or by telephone from OCIC; when a reply may be signed outside the Administrator's office, send a 'bcc' with the Administrator's identifying control number to OCIC; Action Office prepares and sends all required copies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Signature blocks and current official listings
rubrics_metrics.description: Use the provided examples for placement of signature blocks for Officials in the Office of the Administrator and consult current listings for accurate names/titles.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Always consult the Correspondence Management Web site on the HQ Home Page and the latest edition of the HQ Directory to ascertain full names and titles before preparing correspondence and distribution lists.

rubrics_metrics.name: White House referral mail handling
rubrics_metrics.description: Mail referred from the White House requires a direct reply to the writer which should begin with a specified opening and must meet strict acknowledgement timelines.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Replies should begin: 'Thank you for your correspondence of (cite date), to President (name) concerning...' Substitute proper forms when addressed to First Lady or Vice President. White House correspondence must be acknowledged within 15 to 25 business days (depending on subject) unless a different time period is indicated. White House referrals must be signed by the appropriate Assistant Administrator or designee and provide OCIC with two copies of the signed original for processing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Congressional correspondence routing
rubrics_metrics.description: Congressional correspondence is managed by the Office of Legislative Affairs as instructed by NPR 1450.4G and correspondence for signature by Principals must be reviewed by OCIC.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow NPR 1450.4G (Handling Congressional Correspondence and Information Concerning Congressional Activities) and route/sign per OCIC review requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Privacy Act correspondence identification and handling
rubrics_metrics.description: Privacy Act correspondence must be safeguarded per NPD 1382.17E and is any correspondence containing information about an individual plus an identifier (name, SSN, symbol, fingerprint, photo, etc.).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Documents that commonly contain Privacy Act information are listed (SF 171, SF 52, SF 50, financial statements, pay statements). If correspondence contains Privacy Act items removed from a system of records not under a system manager, identify prominently as protected by the Privacy Act using NASA Form 1534 (cover sheet) or the wording from Form 1534 if the form is unavailable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Transmitting Privacy Act correspondence
rubrics_metrics.description: Transmission rules for Privacy Act material differ depending on destination.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Within NASA Center channels: seal in a single envelope/package reflecting the addressee by title and the return address and mark 'TO BE OPENED BY ADDRESSEE ONLY'. Between NASA Centers: send in a single sealed envelope similarly marked. Between other Government and non-Government agencies via USPS: use sealed inner and outer envelopes reflecting addressee by title, mark the return address on both envelopes, and mark the inner envelope 'TO BE OPENED BY ADDRESSEE ONLY'.

rubrics_metrics.name: Destroying Privacy Act correspondence
rubrics_metrics.description: Privacy Act material must be destroyed using approved secure methods.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Forward Privacy Act material to your Center's mail center in a plain brown wrapper or burn bag for shredding or burning. Check NPR 1441.1C, Records Retention Schedules, before destroying.

rubrics_metrics.name: Foreign correspondence special handling and routing
rubrics_metrics.description: Due to political sensitivities and potential technology transfer, all official correspondence to designated foreign areas requires special handling and review.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Designated country lists and transmission guidelines are provided periodically. All correspondence to designated areas requires concurrence of the Office of External Relations. Prepare correspondence in standard business-letter style; use the official country name (e.g., Federal Republic of Germany). Avoid U.S. jargon and acronyms. Transmit correspondence with non-NASA U.S. Embassy personnel through the Office of External Relations, NASA Headquarters. Capitalize the country name in the inside address; USPS requires the country name be in all capital letters on the last line of the envelope or mailer.

rubrics_metrics.name: Forms of address: conventional rules and titles
rubrics_metrics.description: Use conventional forms of address as determined by social and official custom; consult Appendix E for specific forms.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples and rules include: use 'The Honorable' for current and former officials (not used by itself or before a last name alone; when within text, 'the' is not capitalized); 'The Honorable' may be replaced by a title such as 'Dr.' or 'General' but not combined. After leaving a titled position, an individual may retain the title. See Appendix E for detailed models and special cases.

rubrics_metrics.name: Abbreviation of titles and degrees in addresses
rubrics_metrics.description: Do not abbreviate titles preceding full names except Mr./Ms./Dr.; long titles may be abbreviated where necessary for balance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Abbreviate designations of degrees, religious and fraternal orders, and military service branch titles after a name. Type initials of degrees with periods but no spaces (e.g., John Doe, D.D., D.Lit.). Type military service designations in capital letters without periods (e.g., Lt. Colonel Mary Hill, USAF). Do not use scholastic degrees in combination with complimentary titles or military ranks, except 'The Reverend.' Ordering of post-name abbreviations: religious orders first, theological degrees, academic degrees earned in course, then honorary degrees in order of bestowal. Using more than two degrees is unnecessary.

rubrics_metrics.name: Addressing spouse of a distinguished individual
rubrics_metrics.description: A spouse does not share a spouse's official title and should be addressed individually by appropriate title and last name.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: 'The American Ambassador and Mrs. Doe'; for titled spouse female cases use 'Justice Sandra Day O'Connor and Mr. O'Connor'. Not all married women use their husband's name—address as appropriate. Use conventional forms listed in Appendix E.

rubrics_metrics.name: Compound-word policy and preferred forms
rubrics_metrics.description: Use the GPO Style Manual as the first reference for compounding; when not found use the dictionary (Webster's preferred).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: In applying compounding rules, note language trends (two-word -> hyphen -> closed). When a word form cannot be found in GPO or dictionary, default to two words. The appendix provides a representative list of commonly used compound words and NASA preferences (examples: 'agencywide' vs 'Agencywide', 'airmail', 'backup' vs 'back up', 'crewmember', 'double-space/double space', 'onboard/on board', 'Web page/Web site' as NASA preference). The list is not inclusive but indicates common NASA preferences and exceptions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Capitalization of frequently used words at NASA
rubrics_metrics.description: Capitalize specific names of things and lower case general terms of classification; the appendix lists preferred capitalization for commonly used words at NASA.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: 'Agency' capitalized if part of complete name or if used as short form for NASA (NASA preference); 'Attachment' capitalized when specifying (Attachment 1) but lower-case 'attachment' otherwise; 'Associate Administrator' capitalized when referring to a specific person; 'Board' capitalized if part of name or used in place of full name; 'Center(s)' capitalized when referring to NASA Centers. The appendix provides many specific examples and exceptions—use it to determine capitalization in correspondence.
